oauthNotes: OAuth 2.0 via a Google Cloud project. The OAuth client and consent screen ('Google Auth Platform') are configured per project.

generator.by: Claude Code research session (WebSearch/WebFetch) + live probes

composio.note: Composio's managed Gmail app lets you prototype today with no Google review. You need your own app for your name on the consent screen, your own quota, or scopes beyond Composio's defaults. For a public email agent, your own app has to pass the restricted-scope verification below.

summary: Creating a Google OAuth client takes minutes, and testing with up to 100 listed test users is available immediately. A public agent that reads or modifies email requires brand verification, restricted-scope verification and a paid third-party security assessment (CASA), renewed every 12 months.

verdict.headline: Testing is available within minutes. Public access for an email-reading agent requires several weeks and a paid third-party security assessment.
verdict.biggestRisk: Restricted scopes (gmail.readonly, gmail.modify) require a CASA security assessment. It is the longest and least predictable step, and it recurs annually.

paths.name: Public agent that reads or acts on email
paths.whenThisApplies: Any Google user can connect, and you need gmail.readonly, gmail.modify, gmail.compose, gmail.metadata or full mail access. This is the typical AI email agent.

timeToFirstLogin.basis: Project + consent screen + client creation; test users work immediately in Testing status

timeToProduction.basis: Google: restricted verification 'can potentially take several weeks'; community reports 1–3 weeks (lab estimate) to 6–8 weeks for CASA alone

activeEffort.basis: Inferred: privacy policy + domain verification + demo video + justifications + CASA questionnaire/scan remediation

waitTime.basis: Google review queue + CASA lab scheduling and assessment; community reports of stalled Trust & Safety responses

paths.cost: CASA assessment by an authorized lab. Community-reported at about $540 per app for Tier 2 at Google's preferred lab (2024 pricing; confirm the current quote). Renewed annually.

steps.title: Create or select a Google Cloud project
steps.detail: Sign in to Google Cloud console and create a project dedicated to this integration. Use an org-owned account, not a personal one, so ownership survives team changes.

steps.title: Configure branding and audience (External, Testing)
steps.detail: Set app name, support email, logo, home page, privacy policy and authorized domain. Choose External audience. Leave publishing status on Testing and add your test users (up to 100).
gotchas: Test-user authorizations expire 7 days after consent, so refresh tokens must be reissued weekly while the app is in Testing.

steps.title: Create the OAuth client (Web application)
steps.detail: Create a Web application client and add the Composio callback as an authorized redirect URI. Copy the client ID and secret into Composio (Auth Configs → Gmail → OAuth2 → use your own developer credentials).
gotchas: The redirect URI must match the auth config's oauth_redirect_uri exactly.

steps.title: Select the narrowest scopes and test end to end
steps.detail: Choose the smallest Gmail scope set your agent needs (see the handoff kit). Only gmail.send and gmail.labels avoid the restricted tier. Run a test connection with a test user.
gotchas: Google justifications must explain 'why more limited scopes aren't sufficient'. Requesting unnecessary scopes delays review.

steps.title: Verify your domain and submit brand verification
steps.detail: Verify ownership of authorized domains in Google Search Console (DNS record). The home page must be public, and the privacy policy must be on the same domain and say how you access, use, store and share Google user data. Then click 'Verify Branding'.
gotchas: Privacy policy must be on the same domain as your home page.

steps.title: Prepare the demo video and per-scope justifications
steps.detail: Record an unlisted YouTube video showing how a user starts the flow and grants each scope, and how the app uses the data. The agent drafts the script and justifications (handoff kit). You record and upload.
gotchas: The video must show the consent screen with your app name and the exact scopes requested.

steps.title: Submit restricted-scope verification in the Verification Center
steps.detail: Declare all scopes, submit, and answer Trust & Safety emails promptly. Google then asks you to complete a CASA security assessment.
gotchas: Community threads report waits of 10+ days for Trust & Safety replies. Monitor the project owner's inbox.

steps.title: Complete the CASA security assessment with an authorized lab
steps.detail: Engage a CASA-authorized lab (Google points to a preferred partner with a discounted Tier 2 rate). Fill in the questionnaire, run the scans, fix findings, then receive the Letter of Assessment.

estTime.basis: Community: lab estimate 1–3 weeks; developer reports 6–8 weeks

gotchas: Required only if restricted-scope data is stored on or sent through your servers. This applies to almost all hosted agents.

steps.title: Publish to In production and schedule annual re-verification
steps.detail: Once verified, switch publishing status to In production. Set a reminder ~10 months out, because reassessment is due at least every 12 months.

paths.name: Public app that only sends mail or manages labels
paths.whenThisApplies: Any Google user can connect, and you only need gmail.send (sensitive) and/or gmail.labels (non-sensitive). No reading of mail.

timeToProduction.basis: Google: sensitive verification 'can take up to 10 days'; plus brand verification and fixes

activeEffort.basis: Inferred: domain, privacy policy, video, justification

waitTime.basis: Google: up to 10 days for sensitive scope verification

steps.title: Steps 1–5 of the restricted path (project, branding, client, test, domain)
steps.detail: Identical setup. Request only gmail.send and/or gmail.labels.

steps.title: Submit sensitive-scope verification (video + justification)
steps.detail: Submit the demo video and per-scope justification. No security assessment is required for sensitive-only apps.

steps.title: Wait for Google review
steps.detail: Respond quickly to any clarification emails.

paths.name: Internal tool or private beta (no verification)
paths.whenThisApplies: Only people in your own Google Workspace organization use it (Internal audience), or fewer than 100 named testers during development.

timeToProduction.basis: No verification needed for internal or testing use

steps.title: Choose Internal audience (Workspace org) or stay in Testing
steps.detail: Internal limits authorization to your organization's members and skips verification. Testing allows up to 100 listed test users, but their authorizations expire after 7 days.
gotchas: Internal requires a Google Workspace or Cloud Identity org. Personal @gmail.com accounts can't use it.

steps.title: Create the Web client and connect it in Composio
steps.detail: Same as the restricted path's step 3.

requirements.detail: Ownership of every authorized domain, verified via DNS.

requirements.item: Privacy policy on the same domain
requirements.detail: Must disclose how the app accesses, uses, stores, or shares Google user data, including Limited Use compliance.
Shows the user initiating the flow and granting each requested scope.
Why each scope is needed and why narrower scopes aren't sufficient.
From a Google-empanelled assessor, when restricted data is stored on or sent through your servers.
Needed for the Internal audience option.

nuances.title: Testing-mode tokens expire after 7 days
nuances.detail: With External audience in Testing, refresh tokens expire after 7 days unless you only request name, email and profile. A long-running agent loses access every week until the app is verified.

nuances.title: No training AI models on Gmail data
nuances.detail: Google's Limited Use rules prohibit using Workspace user data to create, train or improve AI/ML models (except a single user's personalized model). They also restrict humans reading user data. Your privacy policy and architecture must reflect this.

nuances.title: 100 refresh tokens per account per client
nuances.detail: Creating a 101st refresh token for the same Google account silently invalidates the oldest one. Reuse and refresh existing tokens instead of issuing a new one per agent run.

nuances.title: Unverified apps are capped at 100 new users
nuances.detail: Even before you hit Testing limits, an unverified app shows an 'unverified app' screen and is limited to 100 new users.

nuances.title: Published cost figures are often outdated
nuances.detail: Articles quoting $15k–$75k for Google's security assessment predate CASA (2019–2021). Current community-reported Tier 2 pricing is far lower. Request a current quote.

blockers.symptom: Users see 'Google hasn't verified this app'
blockers.cause: App is External and unverified, or the scopes requested in code differ from the consent-screen configuration.
blockers.fix: Keep requested scopes identical to the declared set. Add testers as test users while in Testing, or complete verification.
blockers.escalation: Verification Center in Google Cloud console

blockers.symptom: Agent loses access after about one week (invalid_grant)
blockers.cause: Testing-mode refresh tokens expire after 7 days.
blockers.fix: Short term: users reconnect. Permanent fix: complete verification and publish to In production, or use the Internal audience for org-only tools.

blockers.cause: Trust & Safety queue or missed email to the project owner.
blockers.fix: Check the Verification Center status and the project-owner and support-email inboxes, and reply to the existing thread. Community reports waits of 10+ days.
blockers.escalation: Reply on the verification email thread; Google Cloud support if you have a plan

blockers.symptom: Asked for CASA Tier 3 instead of Tier 2
blockers.cause: Community-reported: many restricted scopes or domain-wide delegation can escalate the tier.
blockers.fix: Reduce scopes to the minimum and avoid domain-wide delegation unless essential.

handoffKit.title: Consent screen and client values
handoffKit.content:
app_name: <Your product name>   # shown on consent screen
user_support_email: support@<yourdomain>
authorized_domains: [<yourdomain>]
app_home_page: https://<yourdomain>
privacy_policy: https://<yourdomain>/privacy   # same domain as home page
terms_of_service: https://<yourdomain>/terms
audience: External   # Internal only for Workspace-org tools
client_type: Web application
authorized_redirect_uris:
  - https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback

handoffKit.title: Select the narrowest Gmail scope set
handoffKit.content:
Send only → gmail.send (sensitive, ~10-day review, no CASA)
Labels only → gmail.labels (non-sensitive)
Read/triage mail → gmail.readonly (restricted → CASA)
Draft replies → gmail.compose (restricted → CASA)
Archive/label/mark read → gmail.modify (restricted → CASA)
Avoid https://mail.google.com/ (full access) unless you must permanently delete mail.

handoffKit.title: Draft justification for gmail.readonly (edit before submitting)
handoffKit.content: <Product> is an AI assistant that summarizes and triages a user's inbox at the user's request. We request gmail.readonly to read message content the user explicitly asks the assistant to process. gmail.metadata is insufficient because summaries require message bodies, and gmail.labels/gmail.send provide no read access. Data is processed only to provide the user-facing feature, is never used to train generalized AI/ML models, and is not read by humans except with explicit user consent, for security investigations, or as required by law, in line with the Google API Services User Data Policy (Limited Use).

handoffKit.title: Demo video script (≈3 min)
handoffKit.content:
1. Show your app's home page URL in the browser bar.
2. Click 'Connect Gmail' → show the Google consent screen with your app name and each requested scope.
3. Grant access → show the app using each scope (e.g., inbox summary for gmail.readonly).
4. Show where users can disconnect / delete data.
5. Upload to YouTube as Unlisted; paste the link in the verification form.

handoffKit.title: Wire your client into Composio
handoffKit.content:
1. Composio dashboard → Auth Configs → Create → Gmail → OAuth2 → enable 'Use your own developer credentials'.
2. Paste client ID + secret; redirect URI = https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback
3. Copy the auth config id (ac_…) and pass it in your session's authConfigs keyed by the gmail toolkit. Creating the auth config alone isn't enough.
Ref: docs.composio.dev/docs/authentication/custom-app-vs-managed-app

probes.result: Not advertised: clients must be created manually in the console
302 → error page, authError = invalid_client ('The OAuth client was not found'): endpoint live, rejects unknown clients
